c1.note: Comcast's Oct 2026 release names Xfinity as its brand. All variants (F, C, D, B) hold, including the Philadelphia HQ and Nasdaq: CMCSA details.

c3.note: The June 2026 release is datelined Philadelphia and gives Nasdaq: CMCSA.

c4.note: Xfinity is Comcast's residential consumer brand, per the Xfinity site.

c5.note: The Xfinity site lists internet, mobile, TV, home security and home phone as its residential services.

c10.note: Item 1 of the 2025 10-K has this wording, and the auditor report is dated Feb 3, 2026.

c11.note: The auditor report in the 10-K is dated Feb 3, 2026, consistent with the filing date. The 2025 10-K is the latest annual report.

c12.note: The Comcast corporate page states this almost verbatim.

c13.note: The June 2026 Comcast release boilerplate has this wording.

c15.note: Wikipedia says Comcast Cable Communications does business as Xfinity and is a division of Comcast. The 10-K confirms Comcast Cable is a consolidated subsidiary.

c16.note: Xfinity is Comcast's consumer brand for internet, mobile, TV, home security and home phone; the claim's service list (cable TV, internet, telephone, wireless) is broadly consistent.

c17.note: Xfinity's own page says the brand was introduced in 2010 to represent Comcast's residential services; earlier marketing under the Comcast name is well known.

c18.note: Comcast Corporation trades on Nasdaq as CMCSA.

c19.note: Xfinity is Comcast's consumer brand and part of Comcast, with no separate listing, so ownership rests with Comcast shareholders.

c20.note: The 10-K says Class B stock carries 33 1/3% of combined voting power and is non-dilutable, and Brian Roberts owns all of it; 'voting control' is a slight overstatement of a one-third stake but is the commonly used characterization.

c22.note: The Oct 28, 2026 release still calls it 'Comcast's Xfinity', and the planned spin-off leaves Xfinity with Comcast.

c23.note: The release is dated Oct 28, 2026 and opens with 'Comcast's Xfinity today announced the completion of a network expansion project' in Forest, Virginia.

c24.note: The Jun 16, 2026 post says 'Comcast's Xfinity today announced the rollout of same-day WiFi equipment (Gateway) delivery'.

c25.note: The quote is attributed to Eric Jagher, SVP & GM Connectivity at Comcast's Xfinity.

c26.note: The Jun 29, 2026 Comcast release announced the intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky.

c27.note: The release describes a 'tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky'.

c28.note: AP says Philadelphia-based Comcast will continue providing internet services to residential and business customers; Xfinity stays with Comcast.

c29.note: The release subtitle says the separation is 'to be Completed in Approximately One Year'.

c30.note: Michael Angelakis, Comcast's former CFO, will become CEO of Comcast after the separation.

c8.note: Xfinity's own page says its network reaches over 65 million homes and offers internet, 5G mobile, TV, home security and home phone.

c14.note: The saved 'Comcast's Businesses' page has the heading but no Xfinity text. Comcast's connectivity page does name Xfinity as one of its businesses. Medium confidence.

c31.note: The June 29, 2026 release announced the NBCUniversal and Sky spin-off. Comcast said it expects to finish in about a year, pending regulatory and board approvals. I found nothing showing it is complete by Nov 2026. The spin-off leaves Xfinity inside Comcast.

c3.note: Comcast is still based in Philadelphia and trades on Nasdaq as CMCSA. It kept the ticker after spinning off Versant in Jan 2026. The NBCUniversal/Sky split announced in June 2026 is still pending, about a year from completion, and the broadband company stays Philadelphia-based.
